title: General cheat sheet
about:
## My introduction · 40 seconds
I have a master's in AI from Northeastern, focused on robotics and agent-based systems. At Locus Robotics, I work on localization validation and simulation: motion-capture ground truth, simulated sensor integration, and debugging across the stack. Outside work, I'm building a visual SLAM system in C++ and PyTorch, from classical geometry to learned matching and an experimental Transformer solver. I enjoy connecting mathematical understanding to reliable physical systems.

## Locus · measure and diagnose
- **Problem:** Quantify 6-DoF localization and positioning accuracy for mobile manipulation.
- **My contribution:** Built a motion-capture ground-truth framework; analyzed bias, repeatability, uncertainty, and spatial error; published results to an internal web app near real time.
- **Technical depth:** SVD plane fitting, swing-twist decomposition, left-invariant pose error.
- **Simulation:** Integrated IMU, odometry, camera, lidar, and TF with a production localization stack in Gazebo / ROS 2. Designed Docker architecture for local/cloud execution and automated pytest testing.
- **Message:** I make robot performance measurable and failures reproducible. Pick a concrete debugging incident I can explain from personal experience.

## Independent SLAM · mathematical depth and initiative
- Built C++/Eigen SO(3)/SE(3) geometry, essential-matrix estimation, RANSAC, RGB-D pose recovery, loop closure, and Gauss–Newton optimization.
- Trained CNN descriptors: **70.7% vs 58.2%** for SIFT within 8 pixels on a held-out TartanAir sequence: **12.5 percentage points** improvement.
- Developing a Transformer pose-graph solver: **48% lower mean trajectory error** than robust Gauss–Newton across **100 validation graphs with injected faults**.
- Scope: research in progress. Classical optimization remains stronger on clean graphs in several experiments. Semantic-aware solving is a goal; ablations have not established meaningful semantic reasoning.
- Lesson: A better output metric doesn't prove the model uses the information I hoped it would.

## Twelve · hardware and collaboration
- Chemical-reaction test stands: collaborated with scientists on data acquisition and instrument control.
- Built hardware-in-the-loop tests and regression-based anomaly analysis.
- Message: Turn physical behavior into repeatable software checks; work across disciplines.

## Backup examples and personal details
- **Kythera:** SATCOM software, C++ libraries, REST APIs, Docker/Postgres, integration tests, Jenkins/GitHub Actions.
- **iPhone LiDAR:** Modular ROS 2 mapping framework, ICP / learned registration, GTSAM factor-graph optimization.
- **Outside work:** Fencing, building siege engines, mechanical/software engineering.

## When I blank
- “Let me take a second to pick the clearest example.”
- “I don't recall the exact number, but I can explain the setup and what we learned.”
- Answer shape: **problem → my contribution → evidence / lesson**. Pause for follow-up.
technical:
## My solver conventions · checked against the current code
- **Frames:** \(T_{AB}\) maps B into A; vertices are T_WC. The frontend returns T_ji; the graph stores its inverse Z_ij.
- **Graph residual:** \(r_{ij}=\operatorname{Log}(Z_{ij}^{-1}T_i^{-1}T_j)\). Twists are [rho, phi]; updates multiply on the LEFT.
- **Two Jacobians:** Edge-information point residual p_j − q gives \([-I,\hat q]\) (3×6). A graph edge has two 6×6 endpoint Jacobians, effectively \(J_i=-\operatorname{Ad}(T_j^{-1})\), \(J_j=+\operatorname{Ad}(T_j^{-1})\) in the current code.
- **Unfinished detail:** right_jacobian() returns identity. The full derivative includes the inverse right Jacobian of Log; see Math details.
- **Actual solve:** Huber weighting, fixed vertex 0, dense assembly then sparse SimplicialLDLT. The configured run uses LM, with diagonal damping \(H+\lambda(\operatorname{diag}(H)+10^{-6}I)\).

## Rigid-body geometry · my C++ SLAM and Locus work
- **6-DoF:** Three translation and three rotation degrees of freedom. **SO(3):** rotations. **SE(3):** rotations plus translations.
- **My convention:** \(T_{AB}\) maps frame B into A; twists are \([\rho,\phi]\) (translation first); left perturbation \(T_{\mathrm{new}}=\operatorname{Exp}(\delta)T\).
- **Exp / Log:** Convert between local motion coordinates and transformations, allowing small updates that preserve valid rotations.
- **Left-invariant error:** \(T_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}T_{\mathrm{est}}\) is unchanged by applying the same left transform to both poses. State frames and error convention before comparing results.

## Ground truth · my Locus framework
- **Bias:** systematic offset. **Repeatability:** spread across repeated trials. **Accuracy:** closeness to truth. Consistently wrong is still repeatable.
- **SVD plane fitting:** Center the measured points; the right singular vector with the smallest singular value gives the plane normal.
- **Swing–twist:** Decompose orientation into rotation about a chosen axis and the remaining tilt; state the axis and composition convention.
- Ground truth has uncertainty. Check reference calibration, alignment, timestamps, and spatial variation before attributing all error to localization.

## ICP · correspondences and math
**My iPhone LiDAR registration work; general ICP background.** Transform source points into the target frame: \(q_i=Rx_i+t\). Find provisional spatial matches using a target k-d tree:

\[c(i)=\arg\min_j\lVert q_i-y_j\rVert^2.\]

For organized RGB-D, project q_i into the target depth image and check depth / normal consistency instead. Gate distant, occluded, or incompatible pairs; robust weights / trimming limit outliers.

**Point-to-point:** Fix matches, then minimize \(\sum_i w_i\lVert y_{c(i)}-(Rx_i+t)\rVert^2\); the unweighted rigid step is Kabsch. **Point-to-plane:** minimize \(\sum_i w_i[n_i^\top(y_{c(i)}-q_i)]^2\), usually with linearized pose updates.

**Iteration:** Match → gate → solve with matches fixed → update T → rematch. Compose an incremental fit; replace T if solving for the full transform. Initialization, overlap, and geometry matter. A single plane cannot constrain tangential translation or rotation about its normal.

**My learned frontend:** CNN cosine / mutual-nearest-neighbor matching supplies pixel pairs, depth supplies 3D pairs, and Kabsch-RANSAC fits T_ji. That matching is distinct from ICP spatial matching.

## Kabsch · SVD and why it works
**My C++/Eigen implementation:** Fit \(p_k^{(j)}\approx Rp_k^{(i)}+t\). Translation separates: \(t=\bar p^{(j)}-R\bar p^{(i)}\). Center both clouds and form

\[H=\sum_k q_k^{(i)}{q_k^{(j)}}^\top=USV^\top.\]

In code, points are rows: H = pi_c.transpose() * pj_c. Expanding squared distances gives a constant minus \(2\operatorname{tr}(RH)\), so minimizing distance maximizes that trace.

Let \(M=V^\top RU\). Then \(\operatorname{tr}(RH)=\sum_k\sigma_k M_{kk}\). Orthogonality bounds each diagonal entry by 1; matching the SVD directions reaches the maximum. If a reflection would result, flip the smallest-singular-value direction:

\[R=V\operatorname{diag}(1,1,\det(VU^\top))U^\top.\]

This is the global rigid least-squares fit for FIXED matches, without scale or outlier rejection. RANSAC handles bad matches. Coplanar non-collinear points are fine; collinearity leaves a free rotation. My degeneracy diagnostic is σ₂/σ₁.

## Gauss–Newton · my graph residual and solve
Vertices \(T_i=T_{WC_i}\) map camera into world; the frontend returns T_ji and the graph stores \(Z_{ij}=T_{ji}^{-1}\). The edge residual is

\[r_{ij}=\operatorname{Log}(Z_{ij}^{-1}T_i^{-1}T_j).\]

Linearize with a local pose update: \(r(x\boxplus\delta)\approx r+J\delta\). Differentiate the resulting weighted quadratic and set its gradient to zero:

\[H\delta=b,\quad H=\sum wJ^\top\Omega J,\quad b=-\sum wJ^\top\Omega r.\]

J measures residual sensitivity; Ω is edge information. GN drops residual-weighted second-derivative terms. My Huber weights reduce large Mahalanobis residuals.

**Actual configured solver:** LM damping \(H+\lambda(\operatorname{diag}(H)+10^{-6}I)\); fixed vertex 0; dense assembly then sparse SimplicialLDLT. Apply \(T_k\leftarrow\operatorname{Exp}(\delta_k)T_k\). Reject cost-increasing steps and raise lambda; accepted steps lower it. No explicit matrix inverse is needed for the linear solve.

## Jacobians · derivation in my conventions
**Definition:** \(J=\partial r(x\boxplus\delta)/\partial\delta\) at zero update. My twists are [rho, phi] and updates multiply on the LEFT. Differentiate inverse / composition / Log with the chain rule.

For a graph edge, perturbing i gives \(E'=E\operatorname{Exp}(-\operatorname{Ad}(T_j^{-1})\delta_i)\); perturbing j changes the sign. Using \(\operatorname{Log}(E\operatorname{Exp}(\eta))\approx r+J_r^{-1}(r)\eta\):

\[J_i=-J_r^{-1}(r)\operatorname{Ad}(T_j^{-1}),\qquad J_j=-J_i.\]

**Current code:** right_jacobian() returns identity, so the effective blocks are minus / plus Ad(T_j⁻¹), a near-zero-residual approximation. The full right-Jacobian correction remains a TODO.

**Point-error Jacobian:** With \(q=T_{ji}p^{(i)}\) and residual \(p^{(j)}-q\), expand \(q'\approx q+\rho-\hat q\phi\), giving \(J_{\rm point}=[-I,\hat q]\). This 3×6 Jacobian builds edge information; it is different from the graph's two 6×6 blocks.

**Point-to-plane:** Premultiply the point Jacobian by \(n^\top\). With q = (1,2,3), n = (0,0,1), the row is [0,0,−1,−2,1,0].

**Check:** Central finite differences with \(T'=\operatorname{Exp}(\pm\epsilon e_m)T\). Use the same residual sign and manifold update, and vary epsilon to expose sign / frame errors.

## Visual frontend and pose graph · my personal project
- **Descriptor:** feature vector used for correspondence; my CNN learns these. **RANSAC:** fit models from random match subsets, find inliers, refine.
- **Essential matrix:** relative rotation and translation direction between calibrated views; monocular two-view geometry lacks metric scale.
- **Pose graph:** nodes are poses; edges are relative-motion constraints. Loop closure connects revisits to correct accumulated drift; false closures can distort the map.
- **ATE:** whole-trajectory error; alignment convention matters. **RPE:** local relative-motion error. Report mean, median, and failure cases.

## State estimation and sensors · general field vocabulary
- **State:** pose, velocity, often sensor biases. **Kalman / EKF:** predict state and covariance, then correct using measurements; EKF linearizes nonlinear models locally.
- **Innovation:** measured minus predicted measurement. **Covariance:** uncertainty and correlations. Avoid treating correlated sensor estimates as independent evidence.
- **Observability:** whether available measurements determine a state. A smooth or repetitive surface may leave some motion directions ambiguous.
- **IMU:** bias causes drift; gravity and frames matter. **Wheel odometry:** slip / scale errors. **Vision:** texture, lighting, blur, and overlap.
- **Debug order:** timestamps → frames / units → calibration → raw data → residuals → downstream behavior. Replay recorded data and find the first divergence.

## GNC and validation · Locus simulation + Twelve HIL
- **Guidance:** desired path / motion. **Navigation:** estimate state. **Control:** drive actual motion toward desired motion.
- **TF:** ROS frame transforms over time; extrinsics and timestamp validity matter.
- **SIL:** software tested with a simulated system. **HIL:** real hardware participates in the test loop. Validate simulation assumptions on physical hardware.
- **Fault injection:** deliberately introduce noise, bias, dropout, latency, or false constraints; measure degradation and recovery.

## Transformer research · what I can defend
- **Attention:** queries weight keys and combine their values; supports context across graph elements.
- **Ablation:** remove / change a component to test contribution. Retraining without an input is stronger evidence than only corrupting it at inference.
- My demonstrated result is robustness on a specific injected-fault benchmark. Improved trajectory error alone did not prove semantic reasoning or selective use of geometric evidence.

sections.title: Math details
sections.content:
## My learned frontend · the actual correspondences
Code: geometry/best_match.py, WorldModel.get_relative_pose, notes/math_reference.md §14.

The CNN produces unit-normalized descriptors. Compare queries Q with image-j candidates C by cosine similarity: \(S=QC^\top\). Pick the largest score for each query, then require the match to point back to the same query:

\[\hat{k}_n=\arg\max_k S_{nk},\qquad \arg\max_{n'}S_{n'\hat{k}_n}=n.\]

The current config's cosine threshold is 0.8. The matcher refines the peak at subpixel precision and converts feature cells to image pixels with \(u=(u'+0.5)\,\mathrm{stride}-0.5\). Back-project matched pixels with their depth into paired 3D points, then run Kabsch inside RANSAC. CNN similarity supplies the matches; RANSAC tests their geometric consistency.

Frontend output \(T_{ji}\) maps camera-i points into camera j. The graph stores its inverse:

\[Z_{ij}=T_{ji}^{-1}=T_i^{-1}T_j,\qquad T_i=T_{WC_i}.\]

## My point residual · why the sign is [-I, hat(q)]
Code: WorldModel.edge_information; math_reference.md §19. Here q is the UN-CENTERED prediction in frame j, unlike the centered q used in the Kabsch derivation above:

\[q_k=T_{ji}p_k^{(i)},\qquad r_k=p_k^{(j)}-q_k,\qquad \delta=[\rho,\phi],\qquad T_{ji}'=\operatorname{Exp}(\delta)T_{ji}.\]

First-order expansion: \(q'\approx q+\rho+\phi\times q=q+\rho-\hat q\phi\). The target-minus-prediction residual reverses those signs:

\[J_k=\begin{bmatrix}-I&\hat q_k\end{bmatrix}\quad(3\times6).\]

This builds the edge's 6×6 information matrix, not the graph's vertex Jacobian:

\[\Omega_{ij}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{eff}}}{N}\sum_k J_k^\top\Sigma_p^{-1}J_k.\]

Point layout affects rotational confidence and translation/rotation coupling. The current code also floors point-covariance eigenvalues; the older math-reference discussion of this is incomplete. Do not claim a full range-dependent, per-point depth-noise model.

## Adjoint · the frame-conversion step in my Jacobian
Code: PoseSE3::adjoint; translation-first twists give

\[\operatorname{Ad}(T)=\begin{bmatrix}R&\hat tR\\0&R\end{bmatrix},\qquad T\operatorname{Exp}(\xi)T^{-1}=\operatorname{Exp}(\operatorname{Ad}(T)\xi).\]

It changes the coordinates of a small rigid motion. The off-diagonal term couples rotation and translation when the frame origins differ. That conjugation identity is how the graph derivative gets from an absolute vertex update to the residual's coordinates.

**SE(3) reminder:** PoseSE3::exp computes translation as V(phi) rho, not rho itself. Rho equals translation only in the pure-translation case / first-order limit. Log uses V inverse to recover rho.

## Source map · what I checked against
- geometry_conventions.md: T_AB, OpenCV camera axes, [rho, phi], left updates.
- notes/math_reference.md: §§14, 17, 19, 20; checked against current implementation, including newer differences noted above.
- cpp/geometry/src/pixel_to_pose.cpp: kabsch_algorithm and kabsch_ransac.
- cpp/geometry/src/pose_se3.cpp: exp, log, adjoint, right_jacobian identity TODO.
- cpp/pose_graph/src/graph_struct.cpp: residuals, Jacobian assembly, Huber / LM, anchor, sparse factorization.
- python/visual_pose/geometry/best_match.py and pose_graph/world_model.py: descriptor matches, back-projection, edge information, inverse measurement.
- General ICP reference: https://www.open3d.org/docs/release/tutorial/pipelines/icp_registration.html
- General point-to-plane reference: https://docs.opencv.org/4.8.0/d7/dbe/kinfu_icp.html

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.content:
## Geometry & estimation · quick definitions
- **Adjoint:** changes a twist's reference frame.
- **Hat / vee:** rotation vector ↔ skew matrix.
- **SO(3) / SE(3):** rotation / rigid pose.
- **Exp / Log:** tangent coordinates ↔ group element.
- **Jacobian:** residual sensitivity to a local update.
- **Residual:** measurement–prediction discrepancy.
- **Covariance:** uncertainty and correlations.
- **Information:** inverse covariance.
- **Mahalanobis distance:** uncertainty-scaled residual size.
- **Gauge:** arbitrary global reference frame.
- **Observability:** which states measurements can distinguish.
- **Bias:** persistent systematic measurement offset.

## Learning · quick definitions
- **ViT:** Vision Transformer; image patches become tokens.
- **GNN:** Graph Neural Network; messages connect nodes/edges.
- **Transformer:** token processing through attention and MLPs.
- **Attention:** query–key weights combine values.
- **CNN:** shared spatial convolution filters.
- **Descriptor:** feature vector used for matching.
- **Embedding:** vector representation of an input.
- **Token:** one represented input unit.
- **Pooling:** summarize many features into fewer features.
- **Ablation:** remove a component; test its contribution.
- **Inductive bias:** assumptions favored by model structure.
- **Overfitting:** training fit that generalizes poorly.

## Robotics & optimization · quick definitions
- **Odometry:** incremental relative-motion estimation.
- **SLAM:** jointly estimate pose and map.
- **Loop closure:** constraint from a recognized revisit.
- **ICP:** alternate correspondence and local alignment.
- **Kabsch:** fixed-match rigid least-squares SVD fit.
- **RANSAC:** random minimal fits; find consensus.
- **Gauss–Newton:** linearize residuals; solve least squares.
- **LM:** adaptively damp Gauss–Newton steps.
- **Huber loss:** quadratic center; linear tails.
- **ATE / RPE:** trajectory / relative-motion error.
- **SIL / HIL:** simulated system / real-hardware test loop.
- **TF:** time-indexed coordinate-frame transforms.

- Which motion is observable on the hull, and which sensor cues constrain it?
- How do you detect wheel slip, sensor dropout, or estimator inconsistency? What is the safe response?
- What field data / ground truth is available, and how are simulation assumptions validated?

sections.title: Math details
sections.content:
## My learned frontend · the actual correspondences
Code: geometry/best_match.py, WorldModel.get_relative_pose, notes/math_reference.md §14.

The CNN produces unit-normalized descriptors. Compare queries Q with image-j candidates C by cosine similarity: \(S=QC^\top\). Pick the largest score for each query, then require the match to point back to the same query:

\[\hat{k}_n=\arg\max_k S_{nk},\qquad \arg\max_{n'}S_{n'\hat{k}_n}=n.\]

The current config's cosine threshold is 0.8. The matcher refines the peak at subpixel precision and converts feature cells to image pixels with \(u=(u'+0.5)\,\mathrm{stride}-0.5\). Back-project matched pixels with their depth into paired 3D points, then run Kabsch inside RANSAC. CNN similarity supplies the matches; RANSAC tests their geometric consistency.

Frontend output \(T_{ji}\) maps camera-i points into camera j. The graph stores its inverse:

\[Z_{ij}=T_{ji}^{-1}=T_i^{-1}T_j,\qquad T_i=T_{WC_i}.\]

## My point residual · why the sign is [-I, hat(q)]
Code: WorldModel.edge_information; math_reference.md §19. Here q is the UN-CENTERED prediction in frame j, unlike the centered q used in the Kabsch derivation above:

\[q_k=T_{ji}p_k^{(i)},\qquad r_k=p_k^{(j)}-q_k,\qquad \delta=[\rho,\phi],\qquad T_{ji}'=\operatorname{Exp}(\delta)T_{ji}.\]

First-order expansion: \(q'\approx q+\rho+\phi\times q=q+\rho-\hat q\phi\). The target-minus-prediction residual reverses those signs:

\[J_k=\begin{bmatrix}-I&\hat q_k\end{bmatrix}\quad(3\times6).\]

This builds the edge's 6×6 information matrix, not the graph's vertex Jacobian:

\[\Omega_{ij}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{eff}}}{N}\sum_k J_k^\top\Sigma_p^{-1}J_k.\]

Point layout affects rotational confidence and translation/rotation coupling. The current code also floors point-covariance eigenvalues; the older math-reference discussion of this is incomplete. Do not claim a full range-dependent, per-point depth-noise model.

## Adjoint · the frame-conversion step in my Jacobian
Code: PoseSE3::adjoint; translation-first twists give

\[\operatorname{Ad}(T)=\begin{bmatrix}R&\hat tR\\0&R\end{bmatrix},\qquad T\operatorname{Exp}(\xi)T^{-1}=\operatorname{Exp}(\operatorname{Ad}(T)\xi).\]

It changes the coordinates of a small rigid motion. The off-diagonal term couples rotation and translation when the frame origins differ. That conjugation identity is how the graph derivative gets from an absolute vertex update to the residual's coordinates.

**SE(3) reminder:** PoseSE3::exp computes translation as V(phi) rho, not rho itself. Rho equals translation only in the pure-translation case / first-order limit. Log uses V inverse to recover rho.

## Source map · what I checked against
- geometry_conventions.md: T_AB, OpenCV camera axes, [rho, phi], left updates.
- notes/math_reference.md: §§14, 17, 19, 20; checked against current implementation, including newer differences noted above.
- cpp/geometry/src/pixel_to_pose.cpp: kabsch_algorithm and kabsch_ransac.
- cpp/geometry/src/pose_se3.cpp: exp, log, adjoint, right_jacobian identity TODO.
- cpp/pose_graph/src/graph_struct.cpp: residuals, Jacobian assembly, Huber / LM, anchor, sparse factorization.
- python/visual_pose/geometry/best_match.py and pose_graph/world_model.py: descriptor matches, back-projection, edge information, inverse measurement.
- General ICP reference: https://www.open3d.org/docs/release/tutorial/pipelines/icp_registration.html
- General point-to-plane reference: https://docs.opencv.org/4.8.0/d7/dbe/kinfu_icp.html

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.content:
## Geometry & estimation · quick definitions
- **Adjoint:** changes a twist's reference frame.
- **Hat / vee:** rotation vector ↔ skew matrix.
- **SO(3) / SE(3):** rotation / rigid pose.
- **Exp / Log:** tangent coordinates ↔ group element.
- **Jacobian:** residual sensitivity to a local update.
- **Residual:** measurement–prediction discrepancy.
- **Covariance:** uncertainty and correlations.
- **Information:** inverse covariance.
- **Mahalanobis distance:** uncertainty-scaled residual size.
- **Gauge:** arbitrary global reference frame.
- **Observability:** which states measurements can distinguish.
- **Bias:** persistent systematic measurement offset.

## Learning · quick definitions
- **ViT:** Vision Transformer; image patches become tokens.
- **GNN:** Graph Neural Network; messages connect nodes/edges.
- **Transformer:** token processing through attention and MLPs.
- **Attention:** query–key weights combine values.
- **CNN:** shared spatial convolution filters.
- **Descriptor:** feature vector used for matching.
- **Embedding:** vector representation of an input.
- **Token:** one represented input unit.
- **Pooling:** summarize many features into fewer features.
- **Ablation:** remove a component; test its contribution.
- **Inductive bias:** assumptions favored by model structure.
- **Overfitting:** training fit that generalizes poorly.

## Robotics & optimization · quick definitions
- **Odometry:** incremental relative-motion estimation.
- **SLAM:** jointly estimate pose and map.
- **Loop closure:** constraint from a recognized revisit.
- **ICP:** alternate correspondence and local alignment.
- **Kabsch:** fixed-match rigid least-squares SVD fit.
- **RANSAC:** random minimal fits; find consensus.
- **Gauss–Newton:** linearize residuals; solve least squares.
- **LM:** adaptively damp Gauss–Newton steps.
- **Huber loss:** quadratic center; linear tails.
- **ATE / RPE:** trajectory / relative-motion error.
- **SIL / HIL:** simulated system / real-hardware test loop.
- **TF:** time-indexed coordinate-frame transforms.
